items.title: Finite truncated tanh–sinh, exp–sinh, and sinh–sinh trapezoid rules

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §§5.1, 6, and 14, analytic-strip trapezoids, truncation, and tanh-sinh transformation.

references.title: David H. Bailey, A Catalogue of Mathematical Formulas Involving π, with Analysis, Journal of Numerical Analysis and Approximation Theory 50 (2021), no. 2, 108–125
references.locator: §5.3, printed pp. 118–120, tanh-sinh formula (73)–(74), and the exp-sinh and sinh-sinh transformations.

items.statement:
Input a real function $f$ that is continuous on the interior of the selected target domain, a step $h>0$, nonnegative integers $N_-,N_+$, and exactly one domain mode. The finite rule evaluates $f$ only at interior points:

1. **Finite interval $(a,b)$, $a<b$.** Put $m=(a+b)/2$, $d=(b-a)/2$, $s(t)=\sinh t=(e^t-e^{-t})/2$, $c(t)=\cosh t=(e^t+e^{-t})/2$, and $\psi(t)=\tanh((\pi/2)s(t))$, where $\tanh u=\sinh u/\cosh u$. Set $x(t)=m+d\psi(t)$, $x'(t)=d(\pi/2)c(t)/\cosh^2((\pi/2)s(t))$, and $\Phi(t)=f(x(t))x'(t)$.
2. **Positive half-line $(0,\infty)$.** Here $f$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$. Set $x(t)=\exp((\pi/2)s(t))$, $x'(t)=x(t)(\pi/2)c(t)$, and $\Phi(t)=f(x(t))x'(t)$.
3. **Whole line $\mathbb R$.** Here $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$. Set $x(t)=\sinh((\pi/2)s(t))$, $x'(t)=\cosh((\pi/2)s(t))(\pi/2)c(t)$, and $\Phi(t)=f(x(t))x'(t)$.

Return the finite sum
$$T_{h,N_-,N_+}(f)=h\sum_{k=-N_-}^{N_+}\Phi(kh).$$
The algorithm makes no accuracy claim from integrability alone. Analytic-strip and tail hypotheses required for an error certificate are stated in [[thm-double-exponential-trapezoid-error-bound]].

items.title: The reference-triangle Duffy map from a vertex

references.title: Imperial College London, Numerical quadrature, Finite Element course notes, §1.6
references.locator: §1.6, equations (1.11)–(1.13), square-to-triangle Duffy map and Jacobian.

items.statement: Let $S=[0,1]^2$ and let $T=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le1\}$ be the reference triangle. The **vertex Duffy map** is $D:S\to T$, $D(r,s)=(r,rs)$. Its image, inverse for $r>0$, and Jacobian determinant are verified in [[lem-duffy-reference-map-jacobian-and-image]]. The change-of-variables use and endpoint limit for weak singularities are proved in [[thm-duffy-weak-singularity-transform]].

items.title: The first divided difference of a C1 function extends continuously

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §5.19, subtraction of the singular value at an interior pole.

items.statement: Let $a<c<b$ and $f\in C^1([a,b])$. Define $g(x)=(f(x)-f(c))/(x-c)$ for $x\ne c$ and set $g(c)=f'(c)$. Then $g$ is continuous on $[a,b]$.

items.title: A double-exponential envelope bounds the omitted trapezoid tails
items.statement:
Let $A,B,\kappa>0$, $T\ge0$, and let $\Phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be continuous with
$$|\Phi(t)|\le A\exp(-B\exp(\kappa|t|))\qquad(|t|\ge T).$$
For $h>0$ and nonnegative integers $N_-,N_+$ with $N_-h,N_+h\ge T$, one has
$$\int_{|t|>N_-h\text{ on the left, }N_+h\text{ on the right}}|\Phi(t)|\,dt \le \frac{A}{\kappa B}\left(e^{-B e^{\kappa N_-h}}+e^{-B e^{\kappa N_+h}}\right),$$
where the left and right integral means $\int_{-\infty}^{-N_-h}+\int_{N_+h}^{\infty}$. The omitted trapezoid samples obey the same bound:
$$h\sum_{k<-N_-\text{ or }k>N_+}|\Phi(kh)| \le \frac{A}{\kappa B}\left(e^{-B e^{\kappa N_-h}}+e^{-B e^{\kappa N_+h}}\right).$$

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §6, separation of infinite-trapezoid discretization error from omitted tails.

items.title: A sufficiently high power regularizes finite logarithmic endpoint factors

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.4.1–5.4.2, The logarithm and the exponential
references.locator: §§5.4.1–5.4.2, real powers defined through exp and log and the exponential limit at negative infinity.

items.statement: Let $r,m$ be nonnegative integers and $\gamma>r$. Define $u(t)=t^\gamma(\log t)^m$ for $0<t\le1$ and $u(0)=0$. Then $u\in C^r([0,1])$ in the sense of [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]], and $u^{(j)}(0)=0$ for $0\le j\le r$.

items.title: The improper integral of a power at zero

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.4.1–5.4.2, The logarithm and the exponential
references.locator: §§5.4.1–5.4.2, logarithm as an integral and positive-base real powers.

items.statement:
For every real $γ>-1$, the improper Riemann integral of $x^{γ}$ on $(0,1]$ converges and
$$\int_0^1 x^{\gamma}\,dx=\frac{1}{\gamma+1}.$$

items.title: An analytic-strip error bound for the infinite trapezoid sum

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §5.1, Theorem 5.1 and the residue-calculus proof on printed pp. 399–402.

items.statement:
Let $d>0$, $0<a<d$, $h>0$, and let $F$ be holomorphic on the strip $S_d=\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<d\}$ and continuous on its closed substrip $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le a$. Suppose there are $C,\eta>0$ such that
$$|F(x+iy)|\le C e^{-\eta|x|}\qquad(x\in\mathbb R,\ |y|\le a).$$
Put $I=\int_{\mathbb R}F(x)\,dx$ and $I_\pm=\int_{\mathbb R}|F(x\pm ia)|\,dx$. Then the infinite trapezoid sum converges absolutely and
$$\left|I-h\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}F(kh)\right|\le\frac{I_++I_-}{e^{2\pi a/h}-1}.$$

items.title: Symmetric Cauchy principal value by subtraction

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §5.19, the symmetric Cauchy principal value and subtraction of the pole value.

items.statement:
Let $a<c<b$ and $f\in C^1([a,b])$. The **symmetric Cauchy principal value** of $f(x)/(x-c)$, when the limit exists, is
$$\operatorname{PV}\!\int_a^b\frac{f(x)}{x-c}\,dx:=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\left(\int_a^{c-\varepsilon}\frac{f(x)}{x-c}\,dx+\int_{c+\varepsilon}^b\frac{f(x)}{x-c}\,dx\right),$$
where $0<\varepsilon<\min(c-a,b-c)$. [[lem-c1-divided-difference-extends-continuously]] supplies the continuous subtraction remainder; the existence and value of the limit are proved in [[thm-cauchy-principal-value-subtraction-identity]].

items.title: The reference-triangle Duffy map has the stated image and Jacobian

references.title: Imperial College London, Numerical quadrature, Finite Element course notes, §1.6
references.locator: §1.6, equations (1.11)–(1.13), square-to-triangle Duffy map and Jacobian.

items.statement: For the map $D(r,s)=(r,rs)$ of [[def-duffy-reference-triangle-map]], the image of $[0,1]^2$ is $T=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le1\}$. On $r>0$ it has inverse $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y/x)$ and Jacobian determinant $r$; the edge $r=0$ maps to $(0,0)$.

items.title: A power above exponent minus one is Lebesgue integrable at zero

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.4.1–5.4.2, The logarithm and the exponential
references.locator: §§5.4.1–5.4.2, positive-base real powers and logarithm/exponential identities.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For $\gamma>-1$, define $g_\gamma(0)=0$ and $g_\gamma(x)=x^\gamma$ for $0<x\le1$. Then $g_\gamma$ is Lebesgue measurable and integrable on $[0,1]$, with
$$\int_{[0,1]}g_\gamma\,d\lambda=\frac{1}{\gamma+1}.$$

items.title: The double-exponential maps and their change-of-variable identities

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §14 and Table 14.1, tanh-sinh transplantation and its stated scope.

items.statement: The three real maps in [[alg-double-exponential-trapezoid]] are continuously differentiable, strictly increasing bijections from $\mathbb R$ onto $(a,b)$, $(0,\infty)$, and $\mathbb R$, respectively, with the derivatives used there. If the corresponding transformed integrand $\Phi$ is absolutely integrable on $\mathbb R$ as an improper Riemann integral, then the target improper integral exists absolutely and equals $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(t)\,dt$. This is a change-of-variable identity; it asserts no quadrature error for every integrable $f$.

items.title: The Jacobi weight defines a finite positive measure with full support

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3, printed pp. 108–119, Jacobi weight and Gaussian rule hypotheses.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\alpha,\beta>-1$ and define
$$w_{\alpha,\beta}(t)=\begin{cases}(1-t)^\alpha(1+t)^\beta,&-1<t<1,\\0,&t=\pm1.\end{cases}$$
Let $\lambda$ be Lebesgue measure restricted to the Borel subsets of $[-1,1]$, and set $\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(E)=\int_Ew_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\lambda$. Then $\mu_{\alpha,\beta}$ is a finite positive Borel measure, its relative support is all of $[-1,1]$, and every moment $\int|t|^k\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}$ is finite for $k\in\mathbb N_0$.

items.title: The Cauchy principal-value subtraction identity

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §5.19, principal-value subtraction identity.

items.statement:
For $a<c<b$ and $f\in C^1([a,b])$, the principal value of [[def-cauchy-principal-value-subtraction]] exists and, with $g(c)=f'(c)$ and $g(x)=(f(x)-f(c))/(x-c)$ otherwise, satisfies
$$\operatorname{PV}\!\int_a^b\frac{f(x)}{x-c}\,dx=\int_a^b g(x)\,dx+f(c)\log\frac{b-c}{c-a}.$$
The first integral is an ordinary integral of a continuous function.

items.title: A finite double-exponential trapezoid has separate strip and tail errors

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §§5.1 and 6, strip discretization bound and separate truncation bound.

items.statement:
Use one of the modes of [[alg-double-exponential-trapezoid]] and let $\Phi$ be its transformed real integrand. Suppose $\Phi$ has an extension $F$ satisfying all hypotheses of [[thm-analytic-strip-trapezoid-error]] for some $0<a<d$, with horizontal integrals $I_\pm=\int_{\mathbb R}|F(x\pm ia)|dx$. Also suppose $|\Phi(t)|\le A e^{-B e^{\kappa|t|}}$ for $|t|\ge T$, where $A,B,\kappa>0$, and $N_\pm h\ge T$. If $I$ is the target improper integral and $T_{h,N_-,N_+}$ is the finite sum in the algorithm, then it is absolutely convergent as an improper integral and
$$|I-T_{h,N_-,N_+}|\le\frac{I_++I_-}{e^{2\pi a/h}-1}+\frac{A}{\kappa B}\left(e^{-B e^{\kappa N_-h}}+e^{-B e^{\kappa N_+h}}\right).$$
The strip and tail hypotheses are separate assumptions; integrability alone implies neither estimate.

items.title: The Duffy map turns a vertex singularity into an integrable radial weight
items.statement:
Let $\alpha<2$ and let $q:T\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. On $T\setminus\{(0,0)\}$ put $f(x,y)=\|(x,y)\|_2^{-\alpha}q(x,y)$, where $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm. The improper integral over $T$ is absolutely convergent and
$$\int_T f(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\int_0^1\int_0^1 r^{1-\alpha}G(r,s)\,ds\,dr, \qquad G(r,s)=(1+s^2)^{-\alpha/2}q(r,rs).$$
In particular, the transformed radial weight $r^{1-\alpha}$ is integrable at zero because $1-\alpha>-1$.

items.title: The Gauss–Jacobi quadrature rule

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3, printed pp. 108–119, Gaussian weights as integrals of Lagrange cardinal polynomials.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, let $n\ge1$, and let $\alpha,\beta>-1$. Let $\mu_{\alpha,\beta}$ be the finite positive Borel measure with density $(1-t)^\alpha(1+t)^\beta$ on $(-1,1)$ from [[lem-gauss-jacobi-weight-finite-moment-measure]]. Its moments through degree $2n-1$ are finite and its support is all of $[-1,1]$, so it is Gaussian moment data of order $2n-1$ in [[def-gauss-moment-data]]. The **$n$-node Gauss–Jacobi rule** is the general Gaussian rule $Q_n$ for this measure as defined in [[def-gauss-quadrature-rule]]: its nodes are the roots of the monic degree-$n$ orthogonal polynomial, and each weight is the integral of the corresponding Lagrange cardinal polynomial. This definition makes no accuracy or computed-node claim; local well-definedness is supplied by [[lem-gauss-jacobi-rule-data-well-defined]].

items.title: Weighted product Gauss quadrature after the Duffy transform

references.title: Imperial College London, Numerical quadrature, Finite Element course notes, §1.6
references.locator: §1.6, equations (1.11)–(1.13), tensor rule after the Duffy map.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\alpha<2$, put $\rho=1-\alpha>-1$, and let $n\ge1$. For a continuous amplitude $G$ on $[0,1]^2$, let $(z_j,w_j)_{j=1}^n$ be the Gauss–Jacobi rule for weight $(1+t)^\rho$ on $[-1,1]$, and $(\zeta_i,v_i)_{i=1}^n$ the rule for weight $1$ there. Map nodes and weights to $[0,1]$ by
$$r_j=(1+z_j)/2,\quad a_j=2^{-(\rho+1)}w_j,\qquad s_i=(1+\zeta_i)/2,\quad b_i=v_i/2.$$
The **Duffy weighted product rule** is
$$Q_{n,\alpha}^{D}(G)=\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{i=1}^n a_jb_iG(r_j,s_i).$$
It approximates $\int_0^1\int_0^1r^{1-\alpha}G(r,s)\,ds\,dr$. When $G(r,s)=(1+s^2)^{-\alpha/2}q(r,rs)$ for a continuous $q:T\to\mathbb R$, this target is the triangle integral identified in [[thm-duffy-weak-singularity-transform]]. The finite nodes and weights are well-defined by the supplied Gauss–Jacobi rule; the error estimate for such transformed amplitudes is [[cor-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-error]].

items.title: Finite endpoint power substitution followed by Gauss–Jacobi quadrature

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.4.1–5.4.2, The logarithm and the exponential
references.locator: Real powers and logarithmic factors.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §14, variable transformations for endpoint behavior and the need for explicit analytic hypotheses.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Input $a<b$, an integer $n\ge1$, exponents $\alpha,\beta>-1$, nonnegative integers $m_a,m_b$, a function $h\in C^{2n}([a,b])$ in the sense of [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]], and positive integers $q_a,q_b$ satisfying $q_a(\alpha+1)-1>2n$ and $q_b(\beta+1)-1>2n$. On $(a,b)$ define
$$f(x)=(x-a)^\alpha(b-x)^\beta\left(\log\frac{x-a}{b-a}\right)^{m_a}\left(\log\frac{b-x}{b-a}\right)^{m_b}h(x).$$
The logarithms are natural logarithms and their arguments are positive. Put $c=(a+b)/2$, $x_L(t)=a+(c-a)t^{q_a}$, and $x_R(t)=b-(b-c)t^{q_b}$. For $0<t\le1$ set $F_L(t)=f(x_L(t))q_a(c-a)t^{q_a-1}$ and $F_R(t)=f(x_R(t))q_b(b-c)t^{q_b-1}$; set $F_L(0)=F_R(0)=0$.

Let $(z_j,w_j)_{j=1}^n$ be the nodes and weights of the $n$-node Gauss–Jacobi rule for $\alpha=\beta=0$ on $[-1,1]$. Set $s_j=(1+z_j)/2$ and $v_j=w_j/2$. The output is the finite number
$$\widehat I=\sum_{j=1}^nv_jF_L(s_j)+\sum_{j=1}^nv_jF_R(s_j).$$
The inputs $q_a,q_b$ are supplied finite cutoff orders; this definition makes no claim of automatic parameter selection. The conditional integral and error guarantee are proved in [[thm-endpoint-regularized-jacobi-error]].

items.title: Gauss–Jacobi nodes and weights are well-defined

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3, Gaussian nodes and Lagrange weights.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For $n\ge1$ and $\alpha,\beta>-1$, the measure and order-$2n-1$ moment datum in [[def-gauss-jacobi-quadrature-rule]] are valid Gaussian quadrature data. In particular the monic orthogonal polynomial exists, its $n$ roots are distinct points of $(-1,1)$, and the Lagrange weights and finite rule are well-defined.

items.title: Gauss–Jacobi exactness and the derivative remainder

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3, printed pp. 108–119, exactness by orthogonality and the mean-value derivative remainder.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $\alpha,\beta>-1$, and let $Q_n^{\alpha,\beta}$ be the rule of [[def-gauss-jacobi-quadrature-rule]] for $d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}=(1-t)^\alpha(1+t)^\beta\,dt$ on $[-1,1]$. It integrates every polynomial of degree at most $2n-1$ exactly and has positive weights. If $g\in C^{2n}([-1,1])$, and $p_n$ is the monic node polynomial, then some $\xi\in(-1,1)$ satisfies
$$\int_{[-1,1]}g\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}-Q_n^{\alpha,\beta}(g)=\frac{g^{(2n)}(\xi)}{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_{[-1,1]}p_n(t)^2\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(t).$$
In particular, with $K_{n,\alpha,\beta}:=(2n)!_{\mathbb R}^{-1}\int p_n^2\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}>0$,
$$\left|\int g\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}-Q_n^{\alpha,\beta}(g)\right|\le K_{n,\alpha,\beta}\,\|g^{(2n)}\|_\infty.$$

items.title: The Duffy weighted product rule has an explicit bound using pure coordinate derivatives
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, let $\alpha<2$, $\rho=1-\alpha$, $n\ge1$, and let $G\in C^{2n}$ in each coordinate on $[0,1]^2$. Let $\widetilde p_{n,\rho}$ and $\widetilde p_{n,0}$ be the monic node polynomials of the pushed-forward Gauss–Jacobi rules for $r^\rho dr$ and $ds$, respectively. Define
$$M_\rho=\int_0^1r^\rho dr=\frac1{\rho+1},\quad K_\rho=\frac1{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_0^1\widetilde p_{n,\rho}(r)^2r^\rho dr,\quad K_0=\frac1{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_0^1\widetilde p_{n,0}(s)^2ds.$$
Then the rule of [[alg-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-quadrature]] satisfies
$$\left|\int_T\|(x,y)\|_2^{-\alpha}q(x,y)\,dx\,dy-Q_{n,\alpha}^{D}(G)\right| \le K_\rho\|\partial_r^{2n}G\|_\infty+M_\rho K_0\|\partial_s^{2n}G\|_\infty,$$
where $G$ is the transformed amplitude from [[thm-duffy-weak-singularity-transform]].

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.4.1–5.4.2, The logarithm and the exponential
references.locator: Positive-base powers and logarithms.

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the inputs of [[alg-endpoint-power-regularized-jacobi-quadrature]]. Let $F_L,F_R$ be its transformed functions and define
$$C_n=\frac{1}{(2n)!_{\mathbb R}}\int_0^1\widetilde p_n(s)^2\,ds,$$
where $\widetilde p_n$ is the monic degree-$n$ polynomial orthogonal for Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$. Then the improper integral $I=\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ exists, the algorithm's output is $\widehat I=\widetilde Q_n(F_L)+\widetilde Q_n(F_R)$, and
$$|I-\widehat I|\le C_n\left(\|F_L^{(2n)}\|_\infty+\|F_R^{(2n)}\|_\infty\right).$$
Here $\widetilde Q_n(H)=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^nw_jH((1+z_j)/2)$ is the affine image on $[0,1]$ of the $n$-node $\alpha=\beta=0$ rule on $[-1,1]$.

title: Singular and infinite interval quadrature — Examples

items.title: The Gaussian integral on the line with a certified sinh-sinh truncation tail

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §§6 and 14, truncated transformed trapezoids and their hypotheses.

items.statement:
For $f(x)=e^{-x^2}$ on $\mathbb R$, use the sinh–sinh mode of [[alg-double-exponential-trapezoid]]. Its transformed function is
$$\Phi(t)=\frac\pi2\cosh t\,\cosh u(t)\,e^{-\sinh^2u(t)},\qquad u(t)=\frac\pi2\sinh t.$$
Then the absolutely convergent improper Riemann integral satisfies $\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(t)dt=\sqrt\pi$. There is $T>0$ such that $|\Phi(t)|\le e^{-e^{|t|}}$ for $|t|\ge T$, so if $N_\pm h\ge T$, the omitted finite-sum tail is at most
$$e^{-e^{N_-h}}+e^{-e^{N_+h}}.$$
However, the complex extension of this transformed Gaussian does not satisfy the uniform exponential-decay hypothesis of [[thm-analytic-strip-trapezoid-error]] on any nonzero horizontal substrip. Thus this example certifies its truncation tail but does not claim a full discretization-plus-tail error bound.

items.title: An interior Cauchy principal value reduces to a regular integral

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen and J. A. C. Weideman, The Exponentially Convergent Trapezoidal Rule, SIAM Review 56(3), 2014
references.locator: §5.19, subtraction at a simple interior pole.

items.statement: For $f(x)=x$ on $[0,1]$ and $c=1/3$, the symmetric Cauchy principal value is $1+\frac13\log 2$.

items.title: A 1 over r singularity on the reference triangle

references.title: Imperial College London, Numerical quadrature, Finite Element course notes, §1.6
references.locator: §1.6, the reference-triangle Duffy map and Jacobian.

references.title: Christopher J. Bishop, The Riemann Mapping Theorem, Chapter 3 §3, Gauss-Jacobi quadrature lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3, weighted Gauss–Jacobi rules and derivative remainder.

items.statement:
On $T=\{(x,y):0\le y\le x\le1\}$, the weakly singular integral
$$\int_T\frac{dx\,dy}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}=\log(1+\sqrt2).$$
Under [[def-duffy-reference-triangle-map]], its transformed amplitude is $G(r,s)=(1+s^2)^{-1/2}$ with radial weight $r^0$. For every $n\ge1$, [[alg-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-quadrature]] applies with $\alpha=1$, and [[cor-duffy-weighted-product-gauss-error]] bounds its error by $K_0\|\partial_r^{2n}G\|_\infty+K_0\|\partial_s^{2n}G\|_\infty$ with the constants specified there; here $\partial_r^{2n}G=0$.

$$\int_0^1x^{-1/2}\log x\,dx=-4.$$
For example, [[alg-endpoint-power-regularized-jacobi-quadrature]] applies with $n=1$, $\alpha=-1/2$, $\beta=0$, $m_a=1$, $m_b=0$, $h(x)=1$, $q_a=7$, and $q_b=4$.
